newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egyptian shares at record high on good results.
newsitem.headline: Egyptian shares at record high on good results.

text.p: Egyptian share prices hit a seventh record high in as many trading days on Sunday as money poured into the market in response to encouraging half-year results by privatised and partially privatised companies, brokers said.
The Capital Market Authority (CMA) all-share index closed the day at 322.44 points, 2.6 percent up on 314.20 on Thursday. Volume was a hefty 66.99 million pounds ($19.7 million).

The two big privatised real estate companies, Medinet Nasr Housing and Development and Heliopolis Housing and Development, again outperformed the market on widespread confidence in the value of their assets.

Medinet Nasr, the first state company which moved into the private sector through a sale on the stock exchange, last traded at 460.00 pounds, 40.00 pounds up on the day. Heliopolis ended at 565.00 pounds, 45.00 pounds higher.
Commercial International Bank (CIB) was another big gainer, adding 68.01 pounds to 668.00 pounds, according to data from the stock exchange.
The Capital Market Authority, which uses a different method of calculation, said it closed at 600.00 but trading data showed this was based on an unrepresentative transaction.

"We expected the market to keep rising," said Ahmed el-Helw of brokers EFG Hermes. "It's because of the amount of cash coming into the market. Companies are still very cheap and the first half results are very encouraging."
As much as 40 percent of the new investment is coming from foreign investors, he added.
The overall confidence again pulled up some of the recently privatised milling shares, some of which had slipped back before the latest run of increases.
Central and West Delta Flour Mills last traded at 91.00 pounds, up 6.00 pounds, and Upper Egypt Flour Mills at 70.65 pounds, a gain of 2.51.
United Arab Spinning and Weaving/Unirab, in which the state is about to sell off at least another 10 percent, rose 9.25 to a final trade of 95.00.
"It's probably connected with the flotation but I'm not sure it's fully justified," said Helw.
The broker said he expected the market to keep rising through Monday before it takes a rest.
The CMAindex for openly traded firms rose to 507.79 from 502.32 points on Thursday and the index for rarely traded "closed" firms rose to 220.6 from 212.93.
Out of 73 shares traded, 45 advanced, eight declined and the other 20 ended the day unchanged.
